description: Default-deny allowlist for the main window. Grants only the core:event listen/unlisten permissions the vanilla UI actually uses (to receive the streamed `node-log` events). Everything else is denied by omission: no fs, shell, http, process, dialog, clipboard, updater, or `core:default` permission is granted, so those plugin commands are refused at the IPC boundary even though `withGlobalTauri` exposes the JS API object. The app's own #[tauri::command]s (node_start/stop/status, rpc, rpc_tor, wallet_generate/from_mnemonic/address_at/send, vault_status/create/unlock/lock/list/get/put/remove/discard, vault_totp_code (RFC 6238 code from a base32 seed stored as a vault entry — derived in-process, the seed never leaves the backend; fail closed: locked vault/missing entry/malformed base32 → error, never a fake code; the vault status carries the mandatory 'not a TEE until real hardware' honesty field — Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305 software seal, unaudited), vault_keychain_enable/vault_unlock_keychain/vault_keychain_forget (OS-keychain unlock behind the opt-in `vault-keychain` cargo feature — HONESTY: a SOFTWARE convenience, not hardware protection: the vault key is stored in the OS login keychain (macOS Keychain / freedesktop Secret Service) and is released to any process running as this user, not a TEE until real hardware; built without the feature all three return a clean 'not built with keychain support' error, never a silent no-op; every vault status carries the keychain honesty text verbatim in its keychain object), panic, hygiene_scrub (real postern-hygiene metadata scrub, in-RAM bytes only — fails closed on unsupported formats, unaudited), the phone-as-signer requester surface pair_begin/confirm/cancel/list/unpair, login_request/complete/reject, grants_list, grant_revoke, courier_generate_recipient/courier_seal/courier_open (real postern-courier hybrid PQ seal, ML-KEM-1024 + X25519 → XChaCha20-Poly1305 — UNAUDITED reference prototype; crypto seal only in this build: the onion transport stays behind the crate's trait seam with mock-transport tests only, so NO live-anonymity claim and no Tor/network from these commands; recipient keys must be authenticated out-of-band by comparing fingerprints; a bare sealed payload has no sender authentication; every response carries the honesty text), and keys_create/keys_list/keys_sign/keys_remove (real postern-keys ES256 passkey core — UNAUDITED reference prototype; SOFTWARE authenticator: private keys held in app RAM only, zeroize-on-drop, lost on restart — not a hardware key and not a TEE until real hardware; classical P-256 by WebAuthn-ecosystem necessity; no CTAP2/browser integration, so no site consumes these passkeys yet; private keys never cross the IPC boundary; every response carries the honesty text)) are application commands and are NOT ACL-gated in Tauri v2, so they need no entry here. The node/wallet commands (node_*, rpc, rpc_tor, wallet_*) are the 'Advanced / testnet (zero value)' surface: pre-mainnet testnet coins with ZERO value, unaudited, not the primary product surface. The phone-as-signer commands hold no wallet key: they generate only an ephemeral channel keypair and compose a login transcript, kept in RAM (no fs capability, no disk). The vault reads/writes its sealed file via the Rust-side path resolver (app_data_dir), not the fs plugin, so no fs capability is required. Kept window-local (`local: true`, `windows: [main]`) — not a remote/global capability. This hardens the IPC surface; it is a pin, not a security audit.
